Effective Friday, December 5, 2025 (trade date Monday, December 8, 2025), CME Group launched 24/7 trading for new swap-based event contracts. On December 5, iLink order entry was available at the start of the 4:01 p.m. CT open for trade date Monday, December 8. iLink Order Entry is available for order submission. These new, fully-funded contracts provide a straightforward way for clients to take a "yes" or "no" position in a variety of key markets, all with defined risk. Clients can express their views multiple times a day on cryptocurrencies, and key economic indicators including U.S. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and Consumer Price Index (CPI). With positions starting at just $1, these contracts are a simple and accessible tool for market engagement. Additional products to be listed in the 24/7 segment will be determined in the coming months.

As with all CME Group products, these contracts are available to market participants through any Futures Commission Merchant (FCM) that chooses to offer them. The new swap-based event contracts are available in New Release for customer testing.

This topic outlines the necessary information for processing new swap-based event contracts and facilitating 24/7 trading.

Testing and Certification

Certification is not required for customer systems already certified to Market Data Platform 3.0 (MDP 3.0), iLink Order Entry, and Drop Copy 4.0.

New release testing is available from Sunday, 5 p.m. Central Time (CT) to Friday, 4 p.m. CT. Weekend testing is not available. Testing is strongly encouraged.

Mock Trading Session

CME Group offered CME Globex customers an opportunity for Production mock testing on Saturday, November 22. To help ensure readiness and provide an opportunity to transact via our Production systems, customers are strongly encouraged to sign up and test with us starting at 7:30 a.m. CT.

  • To participate in mock trading, clients must register in advance.

  • For additional details, review the mock trading script.

Summary of Impacts

  • Launch of swap-based event contracts.

  • 24/7 Trading - includes holidays, Saturday and Sunday.

  • New Market Segment (90).

  • New Market Segment Gateway (MSGW) and Drop Copy launch.

  • Launch a new MDP 3.0 Market Data - Market by Order (MBO)/Market by Price (MBP) channel, including CME Market Data on Google Pub/Sub - SBE and CME Market Data Over WebSocket API support.

  • New Straight Through Processing (STP) endpoints.

New 24/7 Event Contracts

Pending completion of all regulatory review periods, the following products were listed for trading on CME Globex. Clients in permitted foreign jurisdictions can trade these products 24/7; including weekends (Saturday, Sunday) and U.S. holidays. These contracts are listed with, and subject to the rules and regulations of Designated Contract Markets (DCM).

Location Enforcement

To ensure compliance with regulatory frameworks, CME Globex enforces location-based controls for the new event swap instruments.

Validation Logic

Upon order submission, CME Globex validates the order originator identifier submitted in iLink tag 9537-Location.

  • Pass: If the value in tag 9537 matches a permitted jurisdiction for that specific instrument, the message is processed normally.

  • Fail: If the value matches a restricted jurisdiction, the message is immediately rejected.

Rejection Specifications

In the event of a mismatch, CME Globex will send an iLink Business Reject (tag 35-MsgType=j) containing:

  • tag 380-BusinessRejectReason=100 (Value is incorrect (out of range) for this tag (for example using a value outside defined range of integer))

  • tag 58-Text=Value is incorrect for this tag '9537'

location-enforcement.png?api=v2

Scope

This validation applies only to the following inbound messages for the new event swap instruments:

  • iLink New Order - Single (tag 35-MsgType=D)

  • iLink Order Cancel Replace Request (tag 35-MsgType=G)

  • iLink Mass Quote (tag 35-MsgType=i)

  • iLink New Order Cross (tag 35-MsgType=s)

24/7 trading will not utilize the current CME Globex Friday through Sunday maintenance window. Only products available for 24/7 trading will follow this schedule.

Saturday Maintenance Window Processing Overview

The following section outlines Saturday maintenance processing for 24/7 trading.

Saturday Shutdown and Startup

Shutdown

At the beginning of the maintenance period, client systems will receive a Close-Not Final security status message. Then CME Globex will send the iLink messages toeliminate orders. Next, client systems will experience MDP multicast, TCP iLink and Drop Copy disconnections. At this point, clients should reset their books. CME Group recommends that clients and vendors restart their applications at this time and go through their own restart processes.

Startup

iLink order entry, Drop Copy and market data sequence numbers reset to 1 during the Saturday startup cycle. Client systems will re-establish connectivity to the MDP multicast groups and receive the following startup messaging: 

  1. The Market Data Snapshot Full Refresh (tag 35-MsgType=W) messages on the Market Recovery feed are deleted for the impacted 24/7 channel. Tag 83-RptSeq for Market by Price (MBP) book updates resets to 1 for each instrument repeating group.

  2. CME Globex disseminates incremental real-time market data for that channel and client systems can process the data. A Market Data Incremental Refresh (tag 35-MsgType=X) message will be sent with an empty End of Event indicator if no other information is available.  If session statistics are available, they will be republished via the normal Incremental Refresh messaging:

    1. Current session trade volume

    2. Price levels in the order books

    3. Highest and lowest trade

  3. Security Status (35=f) messages containing market states (per instrument group) will be sent for the 24/7 channel. Then any instrument states that are different from the instrument group state are sent (e.g., Forbidden/Halted instruments).

Pre-registered administrative information will be removed during the Saturday maintenance window. Clients must re-submit their party details definition following the pre-open on Saturday.

Maintenance Window Cancellation

In the future, CME Group may cancel a 24/7 maintenance window in a given week. A cancellation of a future maintenance window will be communicated via the weekly CME Globex Notices.

24/7 Client System Impacts

This section outlines 24/7 client system impacts.

New Market Segment

The instruments available for 24/7 trading are listed on a brand new, dedicated Market Segment. The new market segment ID (tag 1300-MarketSegmentID) is 90.

iLink Order Entry

All existing iLink Order Entry functionality is supported and client systems may leverage existing iLink Order Entry sessions. Client systems must connect to a new Market Segment Gateway, 90, to trade these markets. Additionally, there is a new Order Entry Service Gateway (OESGW) instance. During the Saturday maintenance window, CME Globex will disconnect all clients' sessions on MSGW 90; reset sequence numbers; and cancel resting day orders and mass quotes. Pre-registered administrative information will be removed during the Saturday maintenance window. Clients must re-submit their Party Details Definition following the pre-open on Saturday.

Convenience Gateway (CGW) sessions do not have access to the 24/7 markets.

Drop Copy

All existing Drop Copy functionality is supported and client systems may leverage existing Drop Copy sessions. The new MSGW market segment for Drop Copy sessions is 90. At the beginning of a maintenance period, client systems will experience a TCP disconnection. Drop Copy for CGWs will be unavailable.

MDP 3.0 Market Data

A new CME Globex MBO/MBP UDP market data channel (ID 333) named “Event Contracts II” was launched to support swap-based event contracts. Additionally, CME Smart Stream on GCP SBE and CME Market Data Over WebSocket API supports 24/7 trading.

During weekend trading, client systems will receive preliminary settlements (tag 269-MDEntryType=6) denoted as Preliminary Actual Settlement at Clearing Tick (tag 731-SettlPriceType=00000010). Final settlements (tag 731-SettlPriceType Bit 1: 1=Actual) will only occur during the week.

New Final Settlement Price In Existing SettlePriceType

For event swap-based contracts, the final settlement after expiration will be sent on Globex MDP 3.0. The settlement messages will appear with the following indicators in the incremental message:

  • Preliminary settlement

    • Tag 269-MDEntryType=6

    • Tag 731-SettlePriceType=00000010

    • Tag 270-MDEntryPx= either 0 or 100

  • Final daily settlement

    • Tag 269-MDEntryType=6

    • Tag 731-SettlePriceType=00000011

    • Tag 270-MDEntryPx= either 0 or 100

Settlements and Valuations

A new Settlements and Valuations channel named “Event Contracts Settlements and Valuations“ supports 24/7 trading. The new channel ID is 263 that supports the existing SBE schema version 3. The channel follows the same schedule as the new CME Globex channel, 333 “Event Contracts II“:

  • CME Globex Maintenance Window A: Saturday 2:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m. CT.

A sequence reset occurs during the Saturday maintenance window.

The Tag 731 value incorporates a new "FinalFinal" bit at position 5 to denote the new final settlement message.

For event swap-based contracts, the final settlement after expiration will also be sent on Settlements and Valuations channel. The settlement messages will appear with the following indicators in the incremental message:

  • Preliminary settlement

    • Tag 269-MDEntryType=6

    • Tag 731-SettlePriceType=00100010

    • Tag 270-MDEntryPx= either 0 or 100

  • New Final settlement

    • Tag 269-MDEntryType=6

    • Tag 731-SettlePriceType=00100011

    • Tag 270-MDEntryPx= either 0 or 100

Straight Through Processing

CME FIXML Straight Through Processing (STP) supports trade reports for the 24/7 markets on a new, dedicated endpoint; available on a 24/7 basis.
The existing CME STP FIXML endpoint does not support 24/7 markets. There are no functional or message changes to CME STP FIXML. Client systems should continue to use current URLs (CME STP FIXML - Environment Connectivity) for all other products. CME STP FIX does not support trades on the new markets.

Client systems have a unique x-cme-token for each URL. In case of an invalid or incorrect x-cme-token is detected by CME STP FIXML. Client systems will receive an HTTP error code 406 (Not acceptable) with “The x-cme-token value used in the polling request is no longer valid.” In this case, Client systems should initiate a new Subscription or batch Snapshot.

Reference Data API

Reference data supports 24/7 trading including CME Globex Trading Hours and Holiday Schedules functionality. To support event contracts the following are available on the CME Reference Data API service:

  • The subtype=EVENT value is only eligible for Event Contracts.

  • The fixPayout attribute is populated "null" for non-Event Contracts.

    • fixPayout = The fixed payout amount for any in-the-money strike.

  • Relationship Link - Links the non-tradable swap product to the tradable swap product. The referenceProduct is only present for Event Contracts.

    • referenceProduct

Credit and Risk Management Policies

Weekend Credit Enforcement Policies

This section outlines the credit enforcement policies that are applicable during the weekend trading session.

Limit Management (GC2 and ICC)

GC2 pre-execution risk controls are enforced for all accounts. GC2 limits are set at Execution Firm / Exchange group level. An Exchange Group is a grouping of multiple CME Group exchanges, which trade Futures and Options on various asset classes, including event swaps.

Starting May 11, 2026, GC2 will support unique weekend exposure limits and the existing function to enable/disable weekend trading.

Trading and Product Restrictions

To support this initiative, in the Entity Risk Management (ERM) application, the Inline Credit Control (ICC) Policy function was updated to allow clearing firm administrators to Accept or Reject Event Contract Swaps trading (weekday and weekend) or Event Contract Swaps on Sports (only), at the execution firm level. To trade these products, the clearing firm administrator must select Accept (default selection is Reject) Monday through Friday before 2:00 p.m. CT prior to the start of the next trading session.
Additionally, in the ERM application, ICC Product Restriction Policy function was updated to show firm restrictions for individual Event Contract Swap products as read-only in order to avoid confusion with the policy setting.

In the Risk Management Tools (RMT) application, the Globex Credit Controls (GC2) function includes an “Enable Weekend Trading” checkbox. To enable trading, an authorized firm administrator must select this checkbox and (starting May 11, 2026) specify weekend exposure limits.

Monitoring and Credit Utilization

GC2 utilization is calculated at the Execution Firm/Exchange group level. For Good Till (GT) order on event swaps contracts, utilization is carried over to the weekend session.

FCMs cannot directly view credit utilization during the weekend. FCM utilization threshold alerts will continue to be sent via email.

Mass Quote Protections and Price Banding Functionality

Mass Quote Protections for event contracts do not include delta protections (Delta at Group Code, Delta at Aggregate Product Line, Delta at Product Line). The Mass Quote Protection system treats event contracts as having a delta of zero, so any delta protection selected will not be triggered and should not be relied upon to manage risk. Other Mass Quote Protections, including Quote Fills (X), Executions (Y), Traded Quantity (Z), and Sides are available for event contracts. Price Banding is unsupported.
